fields.subject: index_patient
fields.name: Incisional biopsy
fields.indication: diagnostic evaluation of mixed-density mandibular lesion associated with delayed tooth eruption
fields.finding: Microscopic features consistent with ameloblastic fibro-dentinoma

evidence.quote: Incisional biopsy was done (Fig. 2) and referred to the oral and maxillofacial pathology department, faculty of dentistry, Cairo University

An 11-year-old male child presented to the oral and maxillofacial surgery department, faculty of dentistry, Cairo University with a swelling in the posterior mandible. Radiographic examination revealed a multilocular lesion with mixed radiodensity related to the impacted lower left second premolar tooth. The lesion was large in size extending from the canine to the molars area causing teeth displacement and hindering the eruption of the lower 2nd premolar and one of the lower molars (Fig. 1).

Based on the clinical and radiographic findings, differential diagnoses of odontogenic tumors: ameloblastoma, ameloblastic fibroma, ameloblastic fibro-odontoma, or ameloblastic fibro-dentinoma were made.

Incisional biopsy was done (Fig. 2) and referred to the oral and maxillofacial pathology department, faculty of dentistry, Cairo University, and the microscopic examination revealed cords and nests of odontogenic follicles like enamel organs lined by tall cuboidal to columnar cells with central stellate reticulum-like cells similar to ameloblastic follicles surrounded by juxta epithelial hyalinization (Figs. 3 and 4). The surrounding connective tissue stroma showed primitive immature ectomesenchymal cells resembling dental lamina with areas of dentinoid material (Fig. 5 black arrow) and osteodentin (Figs. 6 and 7 black arrows). The microscopic features were consistent with ameloblastic fibro-dentinoma. Surgical excision of the lesion was done, and the patient was followed up for 1 year without evidence of recurrence.
The microscopic features were consistent with ameloblastic fibro-dentinoma.

fields.subject: index_patient
fields.name: ameloblastic fibro-dentinoma
fields.diagnostic_basis: incisional biopsy histological morphology with dentinoid/osteodentin and absence of enamel matrix/spaces

evidence.quote: Incisional biopsy was done (Fig. 2) and referred to the oral and maxillofacial pathology department, faculty of dentistry, Cairo University, and the microscopic examination revealed cords and nests of odontogenic follicles like enamel organs lined by tall cuboidal to columnar cells with central stellate reticulum-like cells similar to ameloblastic follicles surrounded by juxta epithelial hyalinization (Figs. 3 and 4). The surrounding connective tissue stroma showed primitive immature ectomesenchymal cells resembling dental lamina with areas of dentinoid material (Fig. 5 black arrow) and osteodentin (Figs. 6 and 7 black arrows). The microscopic features were consistent with ameloblastic fibro-dentinoma. Surgical excision of the lesion was done, and the patient was followed up for 1 year without evidence of recurrence.

AFD could be distinguished from other similar lesion like AF and AFO by that AFD exhibit dysplastic or tubular dentin, whereas enamel matrix deposits are found in the AFO but, regarding AF there is no any type of dental hard tissue deposits []. In this case, microscopically, we observed long narrow cords and islands of odontogenic follicles with juxtaepithelial hyalinization. The epithelial strands resided in a primitive ectomesenchymal stroma with stellate-shaped fibroblasts exhibiting long slender cytoplasmic extensions that resembled dental papilla. The lesions exhibited non-tubular dentin entrapping cells in multiple lacunae in close relation to odontogenic epithelium resembling dentinoid. The presence of dentinoid excludes AF tumor. Additionally, there is no enamel matrix or enamel spaces, so AFO was excluded. All of these features are consistence with the AFD.
In the present case the lesion was large in size with no evidence of malignant transformation so, conservative surgical treatment was done with a follow-up of 1 year.

summary.text: An 11-year-old boy presented with posterior mandibular swelling, displaced teeth and impaired eruption around an impacted lower left second premolar.

Radiography and incisional biopsy demonstrated a mixed odontogenic lesion with dentinoid and osteodentin, absent enamel matrix and no evidence of malignant transformation. The final diagnosis was ameloblastic fibro-dentinoma; initial alternatives included ameloblastoma, ameloblastic fibroma and ameloblastic fibro-odontoma, with the latter two explicitly excluded histologically.
Surgical excision followed by one year without evidence of recurrence.
